newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's MAS rejects bid by deputy MD to resign.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's MAS rejects bid by deputy MD to resign.

text.p: Deputy managing director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), Koh Beng Seng, tendered his resignation at the end of last week but it was not accepted, a spokesman for the MAS said on Saturday.
"I can confirm that Mr Koh tendered his resignation but the MAS has not accepted it," the spokesman told Reuters.
He was unable to give any further details and was also unable to say why Koh might have wanted to resign.
The Singapore Straits Times on Saturday reported that finance minister Richard Hu had asked Koh to stay on.
"Yes, I have received his resignation letter. He gave personal reasons. But MAS has not accepted it," Hu was quoted as saying.
Hu said there was no truth to rumours that Koh may have preferred to continue as a consultant to MAS.
The Singapore Business Times on Saturday quoted sources as saying Koh was set on leaving the MAS and would be gone before the end of the year.
Koh is responsible for the day-to-day operations of the de facto central bank.
